content.text:
View A: Four remembered objects—upper: a green circle, right: a red triangle, lower: a blue square, left: a yellow cross. Attention is presently fixed on the left yellow cross; the right red triangle and upper green circle are the next most accessible to retrieve, while the lower blue square is least accessible. Predicted effects of redirecting attention are highly specific: issuing a command for any particular location is expected to move selection to that location almost exclusively, so the system can reliably shift focus away from the current left item to upper, right, or lower on demand.

View B: Four remembered objects—upper: a green triangle, right: a red circle, lower: a blue square, left: a yellow cross. Attention is presently fixed on the left yellow cross; the lower blue square and upper green triangle are the next more retrievable, and the right red circle is less so. Predicted responses to commands are not balanced: most command choices are expected to drive attention toward the upper location, so the view is less controllable—directing attention away from left is likely to bring the upper object into focus rather than reliably selecting arbitrary locations.
